details:
I'm trying to make a pickup object that can be manipulated within a certain volume but goes back to its original position if a player tosses it away or walks off with it. To do this I made a sphere that I attached VRC_Pickup and VRC_Object Sync scripts to and I attached a VRC_Trigger that initiates SendRPC(Respawn) and SendRPC(Drop) when it reaches an OnExitTrigger condition. The OnExitTrigger condition watches a static bounding box with IsTrigger=true.

It's not quite working. When I let go of the pickup object before it leaves the bounding box, i.e. by tossing it with a mouse flick or using both mouse buttons together, it respawns upon leaving the enclosing bounding box as intended. If instead hold onto it and walk it out of the bounding box, it usually stays in my hand or oscillates between the respawn position and grip position.

It doesn't seem to matter what layer I put the enclosing trigger bounding box in as long as the trigger script is configured to watch that layer.

I also tried telling the pickup object to teleport back to another game object instead of respawning but that doesn't appear to change anything.

I tried adjusting the VRC_Pickup AutoHold and Orientation attributes and they don't make a difference.

Making the pickup object IsKinematic=true makes it so I can't toss it anymore but otherwise doesn't have an effect on the behaviors of the triggers.

It doesn't seem to make a difference whether I attach both SendRPC actions to the same OnExitTrigger, or put two OnExitTriggers in the same VRC_Trigger, or use two entirely separate VRC_Trigger components. Adding a delay to the SendRPC(Respawn) to make sure it happens after the SendRPC(Drop) doesn't do anything except make the oscillation between spawn point and my hand slower.

It doesn't make a difference whether I use AlwaysUnbuffered or AlwaysBufferOne.

I think the problem is just SendRPC(Drop). I can't find anything that looks wrong in the other components that I used in this prototype.

Video: https://youtu.be/O9tPkFOFzbw Notice the bizarrely inconsistent behavior when the pickup crosses the edge of the enclosing trigger box.

You can test an instance of the world yourself here: https://vrchat.com/home/launch?worldId=wrld_3e03dc29-007c-46da-a39e-11cbd30fc131&instanceId=0
title: SendRPC(Drop) not working
